dedupe_keys.name: working with natural processes wwnp potential maps for natural flood management in england floodplain reconnection woodland planting and runoff attenuation

description: The Working with Natural Processes maps show where natural flood management measures could be placed in England. The Environment Agency produced them in research project SC150005 as a toolbox for operational staff, first published in September 2017 and revised in May 2024. Seven layers cover floodplain woodland planting potential, riparian woodland planting potential, wider catchment woodland, floodplain reconnection potential, runoff attenuation features for the 3.3% and 1% annual exceedance probability events, and woodland constraints. The floodplain reconnection layer, for example, uses the Risk of Flooding from Rivers and Sea maps to flag low and very low probability areas near watercourses without homes or key services, where reconnecting the floodplain could slow flood waves. Coverage is England; Natural Resources Wales publishes matching layers for Wales. Format and access: vector data through data.gov.uk, OGC API Features, WFS and ArcGIS services. Licence: Open Government Licence; free. Caveats: land ownership, recent buildings and changes to flood risk are not considered, and schemes need local modelling. It supplies the potential layer for nature-based flood adaptation studies. A related catalogue record is the Environment Agency Flood Map for Planning.
